paragraphs: Samson is keeping score in this passage. He says, "I have done to them what they did to me." (Judges 15:11) And earlier he says, "I will not rest until I have taken vengeance upon you." (Judges 15:7) Friend, I think that's what score-keeping does: every hit earns another hit, and nobody ever reaches the last point.

But look at what happens when the ropes come out. "The Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him," and the ropes on his arms became "like burnt flax." (Judges 15:14) The text doesn't say Samson earned that moment. I think that's the point, because the power in the story was never really his muscles, and mine have never been much to brag about either!

Then comes the part I love. The man who just took down a thousand men gets very thirsty, and he cries out, "Must I now die of thirst…" (Judges 15:18) So God opens up the hollow place, and water comes out. (Judges 15:19) Whatever strength you've got, friend, it's on loan, so when you run dry, cry out to the LORD, because Samson's story is NOT done yet.
